## Duplicate set established + disposition plan (AC item b)

**Predicate** — `rebar._commands.recent_creates.normalize_title` (the store's own duplicate-probe normalizer) over all 5,336 live tickets.

Result: **92 colliding normalized titles / 428 excess**. Split:
- **3 groups / 3 excess are FALSE POSITIVES inside the legitimate `Condense comments in <path>` epic** — `__init__.py` vs `_init.py`, `_optionality.yml` vs `optionality.yml` normalize equal. All 6 carry **distinct file_impact** (one path each, matching their own title) and are already closed. Excluded — the epic is untouched.
- **89 groups / 425 excess = the duplicate population.** Exactly reproduces the RCA. **389 open**, 36 already closed.

**Cross-checks:**
- File impact: 0 groups have all-distinct file impact. 72 have identical non-empty file impact, 5 all-empty; the 12 that differ differ only between the pre-burst original and its re-filings (the sweep re-derived impact), never among the re-filings.
- Created: 233 on 08-31, 172 on 09-01, 20 stragglers. Confirms onset.
- Binding store: all 389 open excess bound **1:1** to distinct keys REB-3584..REB-4415. 89/89 canonicals bound.
- Reconciles with the Jira-side count of 321: counting only *open* members promotes an open duplicate to survivor in the 68 groups whose true canonical is already closed. 389 − 68 = 321. **389 is the correct target**; closing only 321 leaves 68 orphaned duplicates masquerading as canonical.

**Canonical rule: oldest member of the normalized-title group.** Supported per-group, not assumed: 84/89 canonicals are already **closed** (work landed pre-burst); no duplicate is `in_progress`; none carries an attestation; only one carries comments the canonical lacks (`jira-reb-3584`, whose own comments already read "Duplicate of unmythical-uninspired-olm" / "Superseded by" — disposition notes, not work). **No work is discarded.**

**Disposition: `--class duplicate` + a live `duplicates` link to the canonical.** Per `gates.py:150` `_LINK_BACKED_DISPOSITION_CLASSES` this is an evidence-backed administrative close: it skips completion verification and the plan-review close gate *by design*, minting a deterministic signed `completion-verifier` attestation (`DISPOSITION duplicate` / `replacement: <canonical>`). **No `--force` anywhere.**

**Ordering** is deepest-first: 309 of the 389 are children of other duplicates, and the child-closure invariant is unbypassable (`transition_close.py:582`).

**Two epics deferred to the operator** — `nauseating-inquiring-ibex` (95da) and `subjective-sudden-goitered` (df55) each hold **legitimate non-duplicate open children** (02aa, 2b0a; 4f66, 5165). Re-homing them to the canonical epic is refused because the canonical is closed. Closing 387 and leaving these 2 open.

**Progress:** 15 closed as `duplicate`, verified. Executed under `REBAR_ROOT` on a throwaway worktree at `origin/main` (4c99403).

comments.body:
## The "reconciler behaved to spec" verdict is NOW UNDER EXPERIMENTAL TEST — do not treat it as settled

Linked `relates_to` bug `anarchic-princely-raven` (`00c1-dc03-1f1f-4ffc`, p1), which is running a
`/rebar-debug` investigation into the DUPLICATE population. This ticket and that one cover two
DIFFERENT populations, and conflating them is what produced the premature verdict:

- **THIS ticket** = the 09-04/05 Jira VOLUME SURGE, explained by the bulk `Condense comments in
  <path>` generator. That explanation is confirmed and the operator has confirmed those tickets
  are expected work under an in-progress epic. Not in dispute.
- **`anarchic-princely-raven`** = the 437 excess DUPLICATE-TITLE tickets, created 08-31 (233) and
  09-01 (172) in six discrete bursts. A separate, EARLIER population whose producer is not yet
  proven.

## Why the exoneration is not yet earned

Two analyses were offered as clearing the reconciler, and BOTH have been withdrawn as
non-discriminating:

1. **Binding distinctness** (5,333 bindings -> 5,333 distinct Jira keys). The binding map is keyed
   by rebar ticket id, so a re-create OVERWRITES the entry and an orphaned create is invisible.
   Proves the map is well-formed; says nothing about duplication.
2. **Per-title Jira-vs-rebar count match** (89/89 duplicate groups equal on both sides). An
   INBOUND echo via `_apply_inbound_create` creates one rebar ticket AND one Jira issue per cycle,
   so it PRESERVES a count match. The test's passing result is exactly what the failure mode
   predicts.

`_apply_inbound_create` does materialise a LOCAL rebar ticket from a Jira issue, so Jira -> rebar
-> Jira is structurally available, guarded only by the binding store and the `rebar-id:` label.
Prior art shows this family of defect is real in this codebase: `robe-creek-zealot` (inbound
create never recorded its binding — fixed in `cda9841`), `nonmystic-topiary-toadfish` (dedup JQL
at `dispatch_one.py:214`), and `serge-silky-colt` / `21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03` (DC index lag makes
`recover_pending` create duplicate issues).

## What is actually established, and what is not

ESTABLISHED: change 2657 is refuted on timestamps (it landed ~7h after onset). The volume surge
is the Condense generator. Provenance of the 437 excess is 405 `creation_channel=python` /
`RebarBotNava` versus 3 `jira`/`reconciler`. The copies cluster into six discrete re-runs, and
the bridge has since run 105 passes producing zero new duplicates.

NOT ESTABLISHED: that the reconciler cannot echo. `creation_channel` is SELF-REPORTED by the
caller, so it is suggestive, not proof of origin. No experiment has yet perturbed a binding or a
`rebar-id:` label and observed whether counts grow.

The reconcile bridge is DISABLED (`disabled_manually`) and stays disabled until the mechanism is
proven by experiment AND the erroneous tickets are cleaned up. Anyone re-enabling it on the
strength of this ticket's current verdict would be acting on reasoning that has already been
retracted twice.

comments.body:
## Update from bug `00c1-dc03-1f1f-4ffc` (anarchic-princely-raven): one half of this ticket's verdict is now EARNED, the other half is WRONG

I ran the experiments this ticket's verdict was asserted without. Two corrections, in opposite
directions.

### 1. "The reconciler behaved to spec" — now EARNED ON EVIDENCE (for the 08-31/09-01 duplicates)

This ticket asserted it; it is now tested. `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_echo_loop_experiment.py`
(real git + real ticket CLI + the stateful Jira fake; no production Jira or store) drove a bound
rebar↔Jira pair through binding loss, `rebar-id:` label loss, both, a create-then-crash orphan,
and DC index lag, over repeated passes:

- **No autonomous echo loop exists.** Every perturbation converges within one pass once the
  perturbation stops.
- The worst self-contained case is **+1 local / +1 Jira, once**. It cannot produce 425.
- Unbounded growth appears only while an external agent re-breaks the binding on *every* pass —
  a driven process, not a loop.

Two independent real-data instruments agree, and neither relies on self-reported
`creation_channel`:

- **Commit authorship.** All 631 CREATE commits on the `tickets` branch in 08-30..09-02 were
  authored by local identities. **Zero** by `rebar-bridge[bot]`. Across all history the bridge
  has authored 24 CREATEs — every one a `[binding-drift]`/`[heartbeat-canary]` monitoring alert,
  never an import.
- **Ticket-id namespace.** `_apply_inbound_create` mints deterministic `jira-<key>` ids
  (`inbound_translate.py:93-97`, confirmed empirically). Store-wide there are exactly **40**
  such tickets, all 06-29..08-24. Of the **495** burst-window creates, **0** are `jira-*`.

Note the count-match test (89/89 groups equal on both sides) is **not** discriminating and was
not used — an inbound echo preserves it by construction.

### 2. Event B's attributed producer is WRONG

This ticket says the 425 duplicates came from "repeated janitor/comment-triage sweeps re-filing
identical findings". They did not. There is no such sweep, and no bulk generator script exists
in the repo.

The producer is **rebar's own Tier-2 plan-replay eval harness writing into the LIVE store**:

`materialize_reconstructed_ticket` (`src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/tier2.py:196-263`)
re-materialises a real corpus ticket (parent + direct children, with their ORIGINAL titles,
descriptions and file_impact) once per replay sample into what it documents as a "FRESH,
throwaway scratch tracker" that "NEVER points at the real ticket store's live state". It builds
that scratch root with `git worktree add`, then calls
`rebar.init_repo(repo_root=scratch_root, force_new_store=True)` (`tier2.py:230`).

A linked worktree has a `.git` **FILE**, so `_commands/init.py:197-199` always returns via
`_init_via_symlink` — **before** `force_new_store` is ever consulted — and `os.symlink`s the
scratch tracker onto the parent repo's real store (`init.py:591`). Confirmed at runtime:
identical symlink result with `force_new_store` True *and* False; the flag has zero effect on
that path.

Direct corroboration, not inference — the harness's own run ledger survives at
`docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/ledger.jsonl` and records **exactly six tier-2 runs**,
the last finishing **2026-09-01T03:36:48Z**. The last duplicate in the store is **09-01 03:36**.
Same minute. Six runs, six bursts. `corpus-2026-08-30.manifest.json` is dated the day `tier2.py`
landed (`1299d9deb6da`, 08-30) and the day before the first burst. `tier2` is referenced by no
GitHub Actions workflow — it is a manual CLI subcommand, which is why it started and stopped.

`caused_by` → **`f1d6-cfcc-a9c6-416d`** (the tier2 harness ticket), class `plan_defect`.

### Net effect on this ticket

- The change-2657 refutation stands (timestamps).
- "The reconciler behaved to spec" stands, and is now backed by experiment rather than assertion.
- **Event B needs correcting**: the duplicate producer was the eval harness, not a triage sweep.
- Event A (the ~1,700 `Condense comments in <path>` tickets, 09-04/05) is a **separate**
  population and is untouched by this work — it remains this ticket's open question.

Full dossier, experiments and RED test are on `00c1-dc03-1f1f-4ffc`.

## Jira-side assessment + bridge re-enable checklist (2026-09-06 ~01:00Z)

Duplicate remediation is COMPLETE (386/386, verified independently — see
`anarchic-princely-raven`). Bridge remains DISABLED. Numbers below are measured, and the
first-pass write plan was verified against **live Jira**, not against the stored baselines.

### Where the two sides stand
- Bridge last mirrored **2026-09-05T14:33:31Z** (`last-pass.json`, `outcome: success`).
  Scheduled runs 15:00-19:00Z never fired; workflow set `disabled_manually` at 19:19:35Z.
  Effective blackout ~10.5 h.
- Jira **REB**: 5349 issues — 4527 Done, 822 not-Done. Bindings: 5333.
- **No durable bridge pause is set** (`refs/reconciler/pause` absent; only
  `refs/reconciler/last-pass` exists). The GitHub workflow disable is the ONLY gate.

### First-pass write plan — 403 transitions (verified live, not from baselines)
| change | count |
|---|---|
| To Do -> Done | 389 |
| In Progress -> Done | 9 |
| **Done -> To Do (UNWANTED reopens)** | **3** |
| To Do -> In Progress | 1 |
| Done -> (archived ticket, REB-4603) | 1 |

398 of these are closes; ~386 are this incident's duplicates, the rest ordinary work closed
during the blackout.

**A raw-drift scan overstates this badly.** 510 bindings carry `baseline.status = null` and
naively read as "needs Done". All 510 were checked live and are **already Done** — zero
transitions. Anyone sizing this from `bindings.json` alone will see ~775 and panic.

### Capacity / ceiling
- Reads paginate at 100/page (`fetch_paging.py`) — REB's 5349 issues are NOT exposed to
  Jira's 5000-row `maxResults` ceiling. Inbound GETs are rotation-budgeted
  (`get_rotation.json`). No query-ceiling risk.
- Writes are the risk. acli is serial at ~4 s/issue, so 403 transitions is ~27 min of pure
  write time **on top of** normal pass work. Recent passes already ran 6-32 min at near-zero
  drift. The workflow `timeout-minutes` is **60**, and **commit-back only persists on a
  COMPLETED pass** — so a `live` first pass can plausibly time out, persist NOTHING, and
  re-attempt the same 403 every hour indefinitely.
- Mitigation is already built in: `bootstrap-throttle` = `bridge sync --max-changes 100`.
  Four throttled passes drain the backlog, each well inside the timeout, each committing back.

Profile ladder (`src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py`):
`dry-run`/`reconcile-check` -> `bridge preview` (0 writes) | `bootstrap-strict` -> `--max-changes 10`
| `bootstrap-throttle` -> `--max-changes 100` | `live` -> uncapped.

### Would this cause a second incident?
Two things must be settled first.
1. **The fix has NOT landed.** Gerrit change **2688** ("Refuse force_new_store inside a linked
   worktree") is `NEW`: `Verified +1`, **no LLM-Review vote**. The leak vector is still open on
   main. The bridge does not create duplicates, but it **amplifies** them: with the bridge on,
   the next tier-2 eval run turns fresh rebar duplicates into real new **Jira issues**. That is
   a strictly worse blast radius than the incident just cleaned up.
2. **3 unwanted reopens.** REB-806/807/808 are `Done` in Jira but `open` in rebar because
   their rebar tickets are synthetic `code_review` test fixtures
   (`rebar~main~Iabc @ rev1`, `~Igap @ rev-gap`, `~Imerge @ mrev`; a 4th, 34f9, is unbound).
   The first pass will reopen all three.

### Re-enable checklist (OPERATOR-GATED — not performed)
Preconditions
1. Change **2688** has `LLM-Review +1` and is **submitted/merged**. Do not re-enable before
   this; the bridge is the amplifier, not the cause.
2. Confirm no tier-2 / plan-replay eval is running or scheduled against the live store.
3. Decide on REB-806/807/808: close the three synthetic `code_review` tickets in rebar
   (so the pass sees Done->Done no-ops), or accept three reopens. Same call for unbound
   34f9-add3-5ee5-4a83.
4. Re-confirm the count immediately before enabling (it drifts as work lands):
   expect ~403 (~398 closes).

Sequence
```
# 1. Dry run FIRST — computes the mutation set, applies none.
gh workflow run reconcile-bridge.yml --field mode=dry-run
gh run watch $(gh run list --workflow reconcile-bridge.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId -q '.[0].databaseId')

# 2. Compare the dry-run manifest against the expected ~403 / ~398-close shape.
#    Then ONE throttled pass (max 100 changes):
gh workflow run reconcile-bridge.yml --field mode=bootstrap-throttle

# 3. Inspect, repeat step 2 until the backlog is drained (~4 passes).

# 4. Only then restore the hourly schedule:
gh workflow enable reconcile-bridge.yml
```

Watch on the first pass
- Change count in the manifest: must be ~403, and **~398 of them closes**.
- **Any CREATE of a new Jira issue.** Steady state here is transitions only; a create means
  an unbound local ticket appeared. Investigate before continuing.
- Pass duration vs the 60-min `timeout-minutes`.
- `last-pass.json` `outcome: success` and `completed_at` advancing — commit-back only
  persists on a completed pass.
- REB-806/807/808 behaviour matches the decision in precondition 3.

ABORT SIGNALS — `gh workflow disable reconcile-bridge.yml` immediately
- The manifest proposes **more than ~450 changes**, or **any** issue CREATE.
- Jira REB total rises above 5349 (+ any issues legitimately created since).
- A pass hits the 60-min timeout (nothing persists; it will loop).
- Any new same-title collision group appears in rebar — the leak has re-fired.
- `bridge fsck` reports `binding_drift` or `store_integrity` problems.

### Housekeeping
`JIRA_API_TOKEN` (Atlassian Cloud, user joeoakhart@navapbc.com) is exported in the operator's
local shell and was inadvertently echoed into an agent session transcript during this
investigation. No external transmission, but **rotate it** as a precaution.

## Report

Operator observed hundreds of open Jira issues, including duplicates, and suspected the reconciler bridge was mass-creating duplicates. Prime suspect was change 2657 (ticket `5c5c`, "Reconcile Bridge ACLI 1200-ceiling outage"), which replaced a single ACLI query with half-open `created` windows.

## Verdict

**The reconciler behaved to spec. Change 2657 is REFUTED.** Two independent, unrelated upstream events explain every symptom.

### Event A — the Jira volume surge (09-04/05)

A bulk LOCAL ticket generator created ~1,700 rebar tickets in ~5 hours, one task per repo file, titled `Condense comments in <path>`. CREATE-event commits per UTC hour on the `tickets` branch:

    19:00  7 | 20:00  62 | 21:00 184 | 22:00 968 | 23:00 318 | 00:00 6 | 01:00 147

All are `ticket_type=task`, syncable, unbound — so every one is a legitimate outbound CREATE. The reconciler mirrored them faithfully.

Per-pass `RECON: outbound_differ` from GitHub Actions (workflow `reconcile-bridge.yml`):

    09-04 15:28..20:27  create=0..4     <- normal steady state
    09-04 21:25         create=138      <- ONSET
    09-04 22:25         create=520
    09-04 23:24         create=1180
    09-05 00:59         create=985
    09-05 01:33,02:34,03:31  FAILED (ACLI 1200-issue ceiling)
    09-05 05:27         create=942
    09-05 06:38         create=746
    09-05 07:27         create=547
    09-05 08:31         create=355
    09-05 09:26         create=156
    09-05 10:25..14:25  create=0..5     <- drained, back to normal

The ACLI 1,200-ceiling outage was a **consequence**, not a cause: the growing not-Done working set crossed the per-query ceiling. Change 2657 landed 2026-09-05T04:35:48Z — **after** both the onset (21:25) and the outage it fixed.

### Event B — the duplicates (08-31/09-01)

425 excess rebar tickets across 89 normalized titles, created 2026-08-31 (233) and 2026-09-01 (172), by repeated janitor/comment-triage sweeps re-filing identical findings (`comment triage: llm core` x9, `a2-1: move last_get_pass rotation bookkeeping...` x12). These reached Jira as REB-665..REB-4415 — days **before** the 09-04 surge. **Zero** duplicate-title tickets were created during the incident window.

## Decisive experiment — the binding store exonerates the reconciler

`.bridge_state/bindings.json` on the `tickets` branch is git-versioned. Entry count per pass:

    09-04 20:35  3626
    09-04 21:48  3764   (+138 == create=138)
    09-04 22:53  3964   (+200)
    09-04 23:51  4164   (+200)
    09-05 01:23  4364   (+200)
    09-05 05:55  4564   (+200)
    09-05 07:02  4764   (+200)
    09-05 07:58  4964   (+200)
    09-05 09:02  5164   (+200)
    09-05 09:46  5320   (+156 == create=156)
    09-05 10:37  5325   (+5)
    09-05 11:32  5327   (+2)
    09-05 12:40  5332   (+5)
    09-05 13:32  5332   (+0)
    09-05 14:33  5333   (+1)

Monotonic, never truncated, and each increment matches the pass's create count exactly whenever it is below 200. Every proposed create produced exactly one persisted binding.

Live binding store (5,333 entries): **5,333 distinct Jira keys; zero Jira keys bound to more than one local ticket.** The reconciler created exactly one Jira issue per rebar ticket.

## Mechanism review (why duplication was impossible here)

- Create-vs-update keys off the **persisted binding store**, not the snapshot: `outbound_differ.py:578` `jira_key = binding_store.get_jira_key(local_id)`, then `:588 if jira_key is None:` -> create, else update.
- A bound ticket absent from the snapshot goes to the UPDATE branch and defers; only a live HTTP 200 GET yields an update (`outbound_mutation_builders.py:255-292`). This is bug `1e08-1a35-0267-4ca6`'s fix — discriminate on MEMBERSHIP, not value.
- Snapshot JQL (`fetcher.py:89-97`) is not-Done UNION the 1,000 most-recently-updated Done issues. Snapshot incompleteness therefore cannot route a bound ticket to create.
- None of `9e65567b79ff`, `e8fbf305057b`, `084e753d30df`, `5ae93de838af`, `a33333b8709a` changed the JQL, the statusCategory filter, the field list, or outbound scope.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Confirm with the operator that the ~1,700 `Condense comments in <path>` tickets were intended, or retract them.
- [ ] Decide the disposition of the 425 duplicate rebar tickets (389 still not closed) and their Jira mirrors REB-665..REB-4415.
- [ ] Re-enable the `Reconcile Bridge` workflow once (a) and (b) are decided.
